content: Erythromycin, rifampin, and certain other medications, such as tipranavir combined with ritonavir, can alter the rate at which other drugs are removed from your body. This can either accelerate or slow down their elimination, potentially affecting their effectiveness. Aspirin, when taken with this medication, may increase the risk of bleeding. However, if your doctor has advised you to take low-dose aspirin (typically 81-162 milligrams daily) to prevent heart attack or stroke, you should continue taking it unless instructed otherwise. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, which could increase the risk of pregnancy. It is important to discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use additional reliable backup birth control methods while on this medication. In the event of an overdose, if someone experiences severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the U.S., you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, regular laboratory and medical tests, such as liver function tests, HIV RNA levels, blood sugar levels, blood counts, and cholesterol/triglyceride levels, are recommended. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store unopened bottles of this medication in the refrigerator. Once opened, the capsules can be stored at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. After opening, the medication expires after 60 days. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This medication may cause side effects such as diarrhea, nausea, drowsiness, dizziness, headache, or vomiting. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off previously existing infections, potentially causing symptoms of those infections to reappear. Additionally, an overactive immune response may occur, which can happen shortly after starting HIV treatment or even months later. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas and decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are not yet fully understood. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare, but tipranavir can commonly cause a mild rash. However, it may be difficult to distinguish between a mild rash and a rare rash that could indicate a severe allergic reaction. Seek medical attention immediately if you develop a rash. Before taking tipranavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to sulfa drugs, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, using machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication may rarely cause an increase in blood sugar levels, potentially leading to or worsening diabetes. If you already have diabetes, monitor your blood sugar levels regularly as directed and share the results with your doctor. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination. This medication may make you more sensitive to sunlight. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. HIV treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting the infection to your baby, and tipranavir may be part of that treatment. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications can affect the removal of tipranavir from your body, which may impact its effectiveness. Examples include apalutamide, macrolide antibiotics (such as erythromycin), and rifampin. Tipranavir combined with ritonavir can also influence the removal of other drugs from your body, affecting their function. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
